models_evaluated: hybrid of decision models and a cheap LLM

links.outcome: Automated judge detection of planted errors and omissions in AI answers, versus frontier judges
links.effect: At the same false-alarm rate Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions vs 48.1% for Opus; Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall; Jev non-inferior on 4 of 6 tasks.
links.quote: Still, omissions were hard for both: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall.

unlisted_practices: Using a low-cost decision-only model as an automated judge of medical AI outputs
Prioritizing audit by judge uncertainty (least-sure answers first) to find more errors than random audit
Setting local cutoffs for automated judges to hold false-alarm rates

screen.practice: automated AI judge for output monitoring with uncertainty-prioritized expert review
screen.reason: Evaluates using a decision-only model as an automated judge/guardrail to monitor and catch errors in medical AI outputs, testing uncertainty-based review prioritization.

primary.practice: automated LLM-as-a-judge / decision-only model auditing with uncertainty-based triage
